nodes.name: Measurability of the measure of a parametrized ball section
nodes.statement: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite dimensional real normed spaces. Let \(s \subset E \times F\) be a measurable set in their product. Let \(\mu\) be an additive Haar measure on \(E\). Then \(\varphi(x, y, r) = \mu \{z \in E\mid \|z - x\| < r \wedge (z, y) \in s\}\) is a measurable function in \((x, y, r)\).
assumptions: \(E\) and \(F\) be finite dimensional real normed spaces
\(s \subset E \times F\) be a measurable set in their product
\(\mu\) be an additive Haar measure on \(E\)
conclusions: \(\varphi(x, y, r) = \mu \{z \in E\mid \|z - x\| < r \wedge (z, y) \in s\}\) is a measurable function in \((x, y, r)\)
nodes.statement_short: The Haar measure of a ball intersected with the $y$-fibre of a measurable set is measurable in $(x,y,r)$.
nodes.label: lem:measurable-meas-ball

nodes.name: Proof of Measurability of the measure of a parametrized ball section
nodes.statement: Consider the set \(t \subset E \times E \times F \times \mathbb R\) given by \(t = \{(z, x, y, r) \mid \|z - x\| < r \wedge (z, y) \in s\}\). Clearly, this is a measurable set. Thus the measure of its sections \(t_{x, y, r}=\{z \mid (z, x, y, r) \in t\}\) is a measurable function of \((x, y, r)\), which is exactly what we need to prove.
nodes.statement_short: Write the quantity as the measure of sections of a measurable set in $E\times E\times F\times\mathbb R$.

nodes.name: Introduce the measurable set $t$ of $(z,x,y,r)$
nodes.statement: Consider the set \(t \subset E \times E \times F \times \mathbb R\) given by \(t = \{(z, x, y, r) \mid \|z - x\| < r \wedge (z, y) \in s\}\). Clearly, this is a measurable set.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the measurable set $t$ of $(z,x,y,r)$

nodes.name: Measure of sections is measurable
nodes.statement: Thus the measure of its sections \(t_{x, y, r}=\{z \mid (z, x, y, r) \in t\}\) is a measurable function of \((x, y, r)\), which is exactly what we need to prove.
nodes.statement_short: Measure of sections is measurable; conclude

nodes.name: Measurability of the set of fiberwise Lebesgue density points
nodes.statement: Let \(E\), \(F\), \(s\), and \(\mu\) be as in \autoref{lem:measurable-meas-ball}. Then the set of points \((x, y)\) such that \(x\) is a Lebesgue density point of \(s_{y} = \{z \mid (z, y) \in s\}\) is a measurable set.
assumptions: Let \(E\), \(F\), \(s\), and \(\mu\) be as in \autoref{lem:measurable-meas-ball}
conclusions: the set of points \((x, y)\) such that \(x\) is a Lebesgue density point of \(s_{y} = \{z \mid (z, y) \in s\}\) is a measurable set
nodes.label: cor:measurable-density

nodes.name: Proof of Measurability of the set of fiberwise Lebesgue density points
nodes.statement: The theorem immediately follows from the non-parametrized version and measurability of the set of fiberwise density points of a measurable set.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the non-parametrized statement and measurability of fiberwise density points.

nodes.name: Lower semicontinuity of ball measure (upper topology)
nodes.statement: Let \(X\) be a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\). Consider the measure of an open ball \(\mu(B_{r}(x))\) as a function on \(X\times\mathbb R\), where \(\mathbb R\) is equipped with the upper topology. Then this function is lower semicontinuous.
assumptions: \(X\) be a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\)
where \(\mathbb R\) is equipped with the upper topology
conclusions: this function is lower semicontinuous
nodes.statement_short: $(x,r)\mapsto\mu(B_r(x))$ is lower semicontinuous when $\mathbb R$ carries the upper topology.
nodes.label: lem:meas-ball-lowersemicont

nodes.name: Proof of Lower semicontinuity of ball measure (upper topology)
nodes.statement: Consider a point \((x, r)\) and an extended nonnegative real number \(m < \mu(B_{r}(x))\) Since the union of the balls \(B_{r'}(x)\) over \(r' < r\) is the ball \(B_{r}(x)\), there exists \(r' < r\) such that \(\mu\left(B_{r'}(x)\right) > m\). Take \(r'' \in (r', r)\), then \(\mu\left(B_{\rho}(y)\right) \ge \mu\left(B_{r''}(x)\right)> m\) whenever \(y\in B_{r' - r''}(x)\) and \(\rho > r'\).
nodes.statement_short: Inner regularity of balls in the radius, then a slightly smaller ball fits inside nearby balls.

nodes.name: Lower semicontinuity of ball measure
nodes.statement: Let \(X\) be a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\). Then \(\mu(B_{r}(x))\) is lower semicontinuous in \((x, r)\in X\times\mathbb R\).
assumptions: \(X\) be a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\)
conclusions: \(\mu(B_{r}(x))\) is lower semicontinuous in \((x, r)\in X\times\mathbb R\)
nodes.label: cor:meas-ball-lowersemicont

nodes.name: Proof of Lower semicontinuity of ball measure
nodes.statement: This lemma immediately follows from \autoref{lem:meas-ball-lowersemicont} and the fact that the upper topology is coarser than the order topology.
nodes.statement_short: Upper topology is coarser than the order topology.

nodes.name: Measurability of ball measure
nodes.statement: The measure of an open ball in a (pseudo) metric space is measurable in \((x, r)\in X\times\mathbb R\).
conclusions: The measure of an open ball in a (pseudo) metric space is measurable in \((x, r)\in X\times\mathbb R\)
nodes.label: cor:meas-ball-mesaurable

nodes.name: Proof of Measurability of ball measure
nodes.statement: This statement immediately follows from \autoref{cor:meas-ball-lowersemicont} and the fact that a lower semicontinuous function is measurable.
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuous functions are measurable.

nodes.name: Existence of a ball of minimal measure centred in a compact set
nodes.statement: If \(X\) is a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\) and \(s\) is a nonempty compact set in \(X\), then for each \(r\) there exists \(x \in s\) such that \(\mu(B_{r}(x)) \le \mu(B_{r}(y))\) for all \(y \in s\).
assumptions: \(X\) is a (pseudo) metric space with a measure \(\mu\)
\(s\) is a nonempty compact set in \(X\)
conclusions: for each \(r\) there exists \(x \in s\) such that \(\mu(B_{r}(x)) \le \mu(B_{r}(y))\) for all \(y \in s\)
nodes.label: cor:meas-ball-min

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of a ball of minimal measure centred in a compact set
nodes.statement: This statement immediately follows from \autoref{cor:meas-ball-lowersemicont} and the fact that a lower semicontinuous function on a nonempty compact achieves its minimal value.
nodes.statement_short: A lower semicontinuous function attains its minimum on a nonempty compact set.

nodes.name: Uniform positive lower bound on ball measures in a compact space
nodes.statement: If \(X\) is a compact (pseudo) metric space and \(\mu\) is a measure on \(X\) that is positive on nonempty open sets, then for each \(r > 0\) there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\mu(B_{r}(x))>\epsilon\) for all \(x\).
assumptions: \(X\) is a compact (pseudo) metric space
\(\mu\) is a measure on \(X\) that is positive on nonempty open sets
conclusions: for each \(r > 0\) there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\mu(B_{r}(x))>\epsilon\) for all \(x\)
nodes.label: cor:meas-ball-gt-pos

nodes.name: Proof of Uniform positive lower bound on ball measures in a compact space
nodes.statement: If \(X\) is nonempty, then we choose \(x\) as in \autoref{cor:meas-ball-min}, then choose \(0 < \epsilon < \mu(B_{r}(x))\). Otherwise, we choose any \(\epsilon > 0\) (e.g., \(\epsilon = 1\)).
nodes.statement_short: Case on emptiness; otherwise take the minimizing centre and any smaller $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Differentiability of iterated derivatives of a C^k map
nodes.statement: If \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\) and \(l < k\), then \(D^{l}f\) is differentiable at \(a\).
assumptions: \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\)
conclusions: \(D^{l}f\) is differentiable at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:Ck-differentiable-iteratedFDeriv

nodes.name: Proof of Differentiability of iterated derivatives of a C^k map
nodes.statement: Since \(f\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\) and \(l + 1 \le k\), \(D^{l}f\) is \(C^{1}\) at \(a\), thus it's differentiable at \(a\).
nodes.statement_short: $D^l f$ is $C^1$ at $a$ since $l+1\le k$, hence differentiable.

nodes.name: Iterated derivative of a product map
nodes.statement: If \(f\colon E \to F\) and \(g\colon E \to G\) are \(C^{k}\) at \(a\), then \(D^{k}(x \mapsto (f(x), g(x)))(a) = (D^{k}f(a), D^{k}g(a))\).
assumptions: \(f\colon E \to F\) and \(g\colon E \to G\) are \(C^{k}\) at \(a\)
conclusions: \(D^{k}(x \mapsto (f(x), g(x)))(a) = (D^{k}f(a), D^{k}g(a))\)
nodes.label: lem:iteratedFDeriv-prod

nodes.name: Proof of Iterated derivative of a product map
nodes.statement: This lemma immediately follows from uniqueness of the iterated derivative and lemmas in the library.
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness of the iterated derivative plus library lemmas.

nodes.name: Standing notation of Section 2.4
nodes.statement: In this section, \begin{itemize} \item \(k\) is a natural number; \item \(\alpha\) is a real number between \(0\) and \(1\); \item \(E\), \(F\), and \(G\) a real normed spaces; \item \(f\colon E \to F\) is a function. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Fixes $k\in\mathbb N$, $\alpha\in[0,1]$, normed spaces $E,F,G$ and $f\colon E\to F$ for the section.

nodes.name: C^{k+(alpha)} map at a point
nodes.statement: We say that a map \(f\colon E\to F\) is \emph{\(C^{k+(\alpha)}\)} at a point \(a\), if it is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\) and \(D^{k}f(x) - D^{k}f(a) = O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha})\) as \(x\to a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is $C^{k+(\alpha)}$ at $a$ if it is $C^k$ at $a$ and $D^kf$ is $\alpha$-Hölder at the single point $a$.
nodes.label: def:cdh-at

nodes.name: C^{k+(alpha)} is weaker than C^{k+alpha}
nodes.statement: Note that this notion is weaker than a more commonly used \(C^{k+\alpha}\) smoothness assumption.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: C^{k+alpha} on an open set implies C^{k+(alpha)} at each point
nodes.statement: If \(f\colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+\alpha}\) on an open set \(U\), i.e., \(f\) is \(C^{k}\) on \(U\) and \(D^{k}f\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder on \(U\), then \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at every point \(a \in U\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f\colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+\alpha}\) on an open set \(U\)
i.e., \(f\) is \(C^{k}\) on \(U\) and \(D^{k}f\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder on \(U\)
conclusions: \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at every point \(a \in U\)
nodes.label: def:contdiffholder-imp-cdh-at

nodes.name: Proof of C^{k+alpha} on an open set implies C^{k+(alpha)} at each point
nodes.statement: The proof follows immediately from definitions.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definitions.

nodes.name: C^{k+(0)} at a point iff C^k at the point
nodes.statement: A map \(f\colon E\to F\) is \(C^{k+(0)}\) at \(a\) iff it is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: A map \(f\colon E\to F\)
conclusions: A map \(f\colon E\to F\) is \(C^{k+(0)}\) at \(a\) iff it is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-zero

nodes.name: Proof of C^{k+(0)} at a point iff C^k at the point
nodes.statement: The forward implication follows from the definition. For the backward implication, we need to show that \(D^{k}f(x) - D^{k}f(a)=O(1)\) as \(x\to a\), which immediately follows from the continuity of \(D^{k}f\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Forward by definition; backward from continuity of $D^kf$ at $a$, giving an $O(1)$ bound.

nodes.name: C^l at a point with l>k implies C^{k+(alpha)}
nodes.statement: If \(f\colon E\to F\) is \(C^{l}\) at \(a\) with \(l > k\), then it is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f\colon E\to F\) is \(C^{l}\) at \(a\) with \(l > k\)
conclusions: it is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-of-contDiffAt

nodes.name: Proof of C^l at a point with l>k implies C^{k+(alpha)}
nodes.statement: Since \(D^{k}f\) is differentiable at \(a\), we have \(D^{k}f(x)-D^{k}f(a)=O(x - a)=O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha})\), where the latter estimate holds since \(\alpha \le 1\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Differentiability of $D^kf$ at $a$ gives an $O(\|x-a\|)$ bound, hence $O(\|x-a\|^\alpha)$ as $\alpha\le1$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of C^{k+(alpha)} in (k, alpha)
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon E\to F\) be a map which is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\). Let \(l\) be a natural number and \(\beta \in [0, 1]\) be a real number. If \((l, \beta) \le (k, \alpha)\) in the lexicographic order, then \(f\) is \(C^{l+(\beta)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f\colon E\to F\) be a map which is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
\(l\) be a natural number and \(\beta \in [0, 1]\) be a real number
\((l, \beta) \le (k, \alpha)\) in the lexicographic order
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-mono

nodes.name: Proof of Monotonicity of C^{k+(alpha)} in (k, alpha)
nodes.statement: Note that \(l\le k\), hence \(f\) is \(C^{l}\) at \(a\). In order to show \(D^{l}f(x) - D^{l}f(a) = O(\|x - a\|^{\beta})\) as \(x\to a\), consider the cases \(l = k\), \(\beta \le \alpha\) and \(l < k\). In the former case, we have \(D^{k}f(x) - D^{k}f(a) = O\left(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\right)=O\left(\|x - a\|^{\beta}\right)\) as \(x\to a\). In the latter case, we apply \autoref{lem:cdh-at-of-contDiffAt}.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis: $l=k,\beta\le\alpha$ by comparing exponents; $l<k$ via the $C^l$, $l>k$ lemma.

nodes.name: Get $C^l$ at $a$ from $l\le k$
nodes.statement: Note that \(l\le k\), hence \(f\) is \(C^{l}\) at \(a\).
nodes.statement_short: Get $C^l$ at $a$ from $l\le k$
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: Reduce to the Hölder-type estimate
nodes.statement: In order to show \(D^{l}f(x) - D^{l}f(a) = O(\|x - a\|^{\beta})\) as \(x\to a\), consider the cases \(l = k\), \(\beta \le \alpha\) and \(l < k\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the Hölder-type estimate; split into two cases
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: Case $l=k$, $\beta\le\alpha$: weaken the exponent
nodes.statement: In the former case, we have \(D^{k}f(x) - D^{k}f(a) = O\left(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\right)=O\left(\|x - a\|^{\beta}\right)\) as \(x\to a\).
nodes.statement_short: Case $l=k$, $\beta\le\alpha$: weaken the exponent
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: Case $l<k$: apply the $C^l$ with $l>k$ lemma
nodes.statement: In the latter case, we apply \autoref{lem:cdh-at-of-contDiffAt}.
nodes.statement_short: Case $l<k$: apply the $C^l$ with $l>k$ lemma
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: C^{k+(alpha)} of the product map
nodes.statement: If \(f \colon E \to F\) and \(g \colon E \to G\) are \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\), then \(x \mapsto (f(x), g(x))\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f \colon E \to F\) and \(g \colon E \to G\) are \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\)
conclusions: \(x \mapsto (f(x), g(x))\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-prodMk

nodes.name: Proof of C^{k+(alpha)} of the product map
nodes.statement: The lemma immediately follows from \autoref{lem:iteratedFDeriv-prod}.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Apply the iterated-derivative-of-product lemma.

nodes.name: Composition of a C^{k+(alpha)} map with a continuous linear map
nodes.statement: If \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\) and \(g \colon F \to G\) is a continuous linear map, then \(g \circ f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\)
\(g \colon F \to G\) is a continuous linear map
conclusions: \(g \circ f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-clm-comp

nodes.name: Proof of Composition of a C^{k+(alpha)} map with a continuous linear map
nodes.statement: Immediately follows from \(D^{k}(g \circ f) = g\circ D^{k}f\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Use $D^k(g\circ f)=g\circ D^kf$ for linear $g$.

nodes.name: Linear composition lemma is a special case of the composition lemma
nodes.statement: \autoref{lem:cdh-at-clm-comp} immediately follows from a more general \autoref{lem:cdh-at-comp} below.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point

nodes.name: Derivative of a C^{k+1+(alpha)} map is C^{k+(alpha)}
nodes.statement: If \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+1+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\), then \(Df\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+1+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\)
conclusions: \(Df\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-fderiv

nodes.name: Proof of Derivative of a C^{k+1+(alpha)} map is C^{k+(alpha)}
nodes.statement: The lemma immediately follows from \(D^{k+1}f = D(D^{k}f)\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Use $D^{k+1}f=D(D^kf)$.

nodes.name: Iterated derivative of a C^{k+l+(alpha)} map
nodes.statement: If \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+l+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\), then \(D^{k}f\) is \(C^{l+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: \(f \colon E \to F\) is \(C^{k+l+(\alpha)}\) at \(a \in E\)
conclusions: \(D^{k}f\) is \(C^{l+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-iteratedFDeriv

nodes.name: Proof of Iterated derivative of a C^{k+l+(alpha)} map
nodes.statement: The proof by induction on \(k\) using \autoref{lem:cdh-at-fderiv} and \autoref{lem:cdh-at-clm-comp}. The latter lemma is required, because \(D^{k+1}f\) and \(D(D^{k} f)\) have different types in Lean, and are related by a continuous linear equivalence.
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$ using the derivative lemma and composition with a continuous linear equivalence.

nodes.name: Composition of C^{k+(alpha)} maps
nodes.statement: Consider \(g\colon F \to G\), \(f\colon E \to F\), and \(a \in E\) such that \(g\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(f(a)\) and \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\), where \(k > 0\) and \(\alpha \in [0, 1]\). Then \(g\circ f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\).
nodes.section: 2.4 \(C^{k}\) maps with locally Hölder derivatives at a point
assumptions: Consider \(g\colon F \to G\), \(f\colon E \to F\), and \(a \in E\)
\(g\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(f(a)\)
\(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
conclusions: \(g\circ f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\)
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-comp

nodes.name: Proof of Composition of C^{k+(alpha)} maps
nodes.statement: Since \(g\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(f(a)\) and \(f\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\), the composition \(g\circ f\) is \(C^{k}\) at \(a\). Let us show that \(D^{k}(g\circ f)(x) - D^{k}(g\circ f)(a) = O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha})\) as \(x\to \alpha\). Due to the Faa Di Bruno formula, we have \[ D^k(g\circ f)(a) = \sum_{P}TC_{P}\left(D^{|P|}g(f(a)), D^{|P_{0}|}f(a), \dots, D^{\left|P_{|P|-1}\right|}f(a)\right), \] where the sum is taken over all partitions \(P\) of \(0, \dots, k - 1\) into disjoint sets, and \(TC_{P}\) is a continuous multilinear map in all \(|P|+1\) variables which depends only on the normed spaces and the partition \(P\). Subtracting these expressions, we see that it suffices to show that for each partition \(P\), we have \begin{align*} TC_{P}&\left(D^{|P|}g(f(x)), D^{|P_{0}|}f(x), \dots, D^{\left|P_{|P|-1}\right|}f(x)\right) -\\ &TC_{P}\left(D^{|P|}g(f(a)), D^{|P_{0}|}f(a), \dots, D^{\left|P_{|P|-1}\right|}f(a)\right) =\\ &O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}). \end{align*} Since \(k > 0\), the function \(f\) is Lipschitz near \(a\), thus \(f(x) - f(a) = O(x - a)\), \(D^{|P|}g(f(x)) - D^{|P|}g(f(a)) = O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha})\), and \(D^{|P_{j}|}f(x) - D^{|P_{j}|}f(a) = O(\|x - a\|^{\alpha})\). Now, the goal follows from the fact that a continuous multilinear map is locally Lipschitz.

nodes.name: Proof of Inverse function theorem for C^{k+(alpha)} maps
nodes.statement: From the usual inverse function theorem for \(C^{k}\) maps, we know that \(g=f^{-1}\) is \(C^{k}\) in a neighborhood of \(f(a)\). Thus we only need to show that \(D^{k}g(y)-D^{k}g(f(a)) = O\left(\|y - f(a)\|^{\alpha}\right)\) as \(y \to f(a)\). Equivalently, we need to show that \(D^{k}g(f(x)) - D^{k}g(f(a)) = O\left(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\right)\) as \(x\to a\). Consider the cases \(k = 1\) and \(k > 1\). \textbf{Case I:\@\(k = 1\)}. In this case we need to show that \(g'(f(x)) - g'(f(a)) = O\left(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\right)\) as \(x\to a\). This immediately follows from \(g'(f(x)) = {f'(x)}^{-1}\), a similar estimate on \(f'(x) - f'(a)\), and differentiability of the inversion of a continuous linear equivalence. \textbf{Case II:\@\(k > 1\)}. Apply the Faa Di Bruno formula to find \(D^{k}(g \circ f) = D^{k} id =0\). Note that the only term in the RHS of the Faa Di Bruno formula that depends on \(D^{k}g\) is \(D^{k}g\circ_{k} f'\), where \(\circ_{k}\) means composition of a continuous multilinear map \(D^{k}g\) and a continuous linear map \(f'\). Similarly, the only term that depends on \(D^{k}f(x)\) is \(g'(f(x))\circ D^{k}f(x)\). All other derivatives of \(f\) and \(g\) are differentiable, hence Lipschitz continuous near \(a\) and \(f(a)\), respectively. Therefore, \(D^{k}g(f(x))\circ_{k}f'(x) - D^{k}g(f(a))\circ_{k}f'(a)=O\left(\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\right)\) as \(x\to a\). This immediately implies the required estimate.

nodes.name: Implicit function theorem for C^{k+(alpha)} maps (kernel form)
nodes.statement: Let \(E\), \(F\), and \(G\) be finite dimensional real normed spaces. nodes.name: Moreira chart
nodes.statement: Consider a natural number \(k\), a real number \(\alpha\in[0, 1]\), a set \(s \subset E \times \mathbb R^{n}\), and its open neighborhood \(U\). A \emph{Moreira chart} of depth \(l \le k\) consists of \begin{itemize} \item an antitone sequence of dimensions \(n = d_{0}\ge d_{1}\ge \dots \ge d_{l}\); \item for each \(i \le l\), an open ball \(B_{i} \subset E\) and an open ball \(V_{i}\subset \mathbb R^{d_{i}}\); \item for each \(i \le l\), a set \(t_{i}\subset B_{i}\times V_{i}\); \item for each \(i < l\), a map \(\psi_{i}\colon E\times \mathbb R^{d_{i+1}} \to \mathbb R^{d_{i}}\) \end{itemize} such that \begin{itemize} \item \(B_{0}\times V_{0}\subset U\) and \(t_{0}\subset s\); \item each map \((x, y) \mapsto (x, \psi_{i}(x, y))\) maps \(B_{i+1}\times V_{i+1}\) to \(B_{i}\times V_{i}\) and \(t_{i+1}\) to \(t_{i}\); \item each \(\psi_{i}\) is \(C^{k-i+(\alpha)}\) on \((t_{i+1}, B_{i+1}\times V_{i+1})\); \item each \(\psi_{i}(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V_{i+1}\) for each \(x \in B_{i + 1}\); \item for any map \(f\colon E\times \mathbb R^{d_{i}} \to \mathbb R\) that is \(C^{k-i+(\alpha)}\) on \((t_{i}, B_{i}\times V_{i})\) and vanishes on \(t_{i}\), the differential \(D_{2}(f \circ \psi_{i})\) vanishes on \(t_{i+1}\). \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A depth-$l$ tower of balls, sets $t_i$ and expanding $C^{k-i+(\alpha)}$ maps $\psi_i$ reducing dimension while killing $D_2$ of functions vanishing on $t_i$.
nodes.label: def:moreira-chart

nodes.name: Moreira chart maps Psi_i
nodes.statement: Given a Moreira chart, for each \(i \le l\) we define the map \(\Psi_{i}\colon E\times \mathbb R^{d_{i}}\to \mathbb R^{n}\) by \(\Psi_{0}(x, y)=y\) and \(\Psi_{i+1}(x, y)=\Psi_{i}(x, \psi_{i}(x, y))\).
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi_i$ is the composite of the chart maps $\psi_0,\dots,\psi_{i-1}$.
nodes.label: def:moreira-chart-map

nodes.name: Properties of Moreira chart maps
nodes.statement: Given a \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) Moreira chart, \begin{itemize} \item each map \(\Psi_{i}\) is \(C^{k-i+(\alpha)}\) on \((t_{i+1}, B_{i+1}\times V_{i+1})\); \item \((x, \Psi_{i}(x, y)) \in s\) whenever \((x, y) \in t_{i+1}\); \item each \(\Psi_{i}(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V_{i+1}\) for each \(x\in B_{i+1}\). \end{itemize}
assumptions: Given a \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) Moreira chart
conclusions: each map \(\Psi_{i}\) is \(C^{k-i+(\alpha)}\) on \((t_{i+1}, B_{i+1}\times V_{i+1})\)
\((x, \Psi_{i}(x, y)) \in s\) whenever \((x, y) \in t_{i+1}\)
each \(\Psi_{i}(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V_{i+1}\) for each \(x\in B_{i+1}\)
nodes.label: lem:moreira-chart-map-props

nodes.name: Increment bound from vanishing directional derivative on a large set
nodes.statement: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be a real normed spaces. Consider a function \(f\colon E\to F\), points \(a, b \in E\), and numbers \(C\ge 0\), \(\delta\ge 0\), \(r \ge 0\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(f\) is differentiable on \([a, b]\); \item \(\|D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a))\| \le Ct^{r}{\|b - a\|}^{1+r}\); \item the set of \(t\) such that \(D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a)) = 0\) has measure at least \(1 - \delta\). \end{itemize} Then \(\|f(b) - f(a)\| \le C\delta{\|b - a\|}^{1+r}\).
assumptions: \(E\) and \(F\) be a real normed spaces
\(f\) is differentiable on \([a, b]\)
the set of \(t\) such that \(D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a)) = 0\) has measure at least \(1 - \delta\)
nodes.statement_short: If the directional derivative along $[a,b]$ is bounded by $Ct^r\|b-a\|^{1+r}$ and vanishes on measure $\ge1-\delta$, then $\|f(b)-f(a)\|\le C\delta\|b-a\|^{1+r}$.
nodes.label: lem:cdh-at-sub-affine-le-of-meas

nodes.name: Proof of Increment bound from vanishing directional derivative on a large set
nodes.statement: Let \(s\) be the set of \(t \in [0, 1]\) such that \(D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a)) \ne 0\). We have \begin{align*} \|f(b) - f(a)\| &= \left|\int_{0}^{1} D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a))\,dt\right| \\ &= \left|\int_{t\in s} D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a))\,dt\right| \\ &\le \int_{t \in s} Ct^{r}{\|b - a\|}^{1+r}\,dt \\ &= C{\|b - a\|}^{1+r} \int_{t \in s}t^{r}\,dt \\ &\le C{\|b - a\|}^{1+r} \lambda(s) \\ &\le C\delta {\|b - a\|}^{1+r} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment, integrating only over the set where the derivative is nonzero.

nodes.name: Improved constant in the increment bound
nodes.statement: The constant can be improved, but probably we don't need this. In order to do this, we need to show that \[ \int_{t \in s}t^{r}\,dt \le \int_{1 - \delta}^{1} t^{r}\,dt = \frac{1 - {(1 - \delta)}^{r + 1}}{r + 1}. \]

nodes.name: Increment bound from vanishing derivative on a large set (full derivative)
nodes.statement: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be a real normed spaces. Consider a function \(f\colon E\to F\), points \(a, b \in E\), and numbers \(C\ge 0\), \(\delta\ge 0\), \(r \ge 0\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(f\) is differentiable on \([a, b]\); \item \(\|Df(a + t(b - a))\| \le Ct^{r}{\|b - a\|}^r\); \item the set of \(t\) such that \(D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a)) = 0\) has measure at least \(1 - \delta\). \end{itemize} Then \(\|f(b) - f(a)\| \le C\delta{\|b - a\|}^{1+r}\).
assumptions: \(E\) and \(F\) be a real normed spaces
\(f\) is differentiable on \([a, b]\)
the set of \(t\) such that \(D_{b - a}f(a + t(b - a)) = 0\) has measure at least \(1 - \delta\)
nodes.label: cor:cdh-at-sub-le-of-meas-fderiv

nodes.name: Proof of Increment bound from vanishing derivative on a large set (full derivative)
nodes.statement: This lemma immediately follows from \autoref{lem:cdh-at-sub-affine-le-of-meas} and the fact that \(\|D_{b-a}f(x)\|\le \|Df(x)\|\times\|b - a\|\).
nodes.statement_short: Bound the directional derivative by $\|Df\|\,\|b-a\|$ and apply the previous lemma.

nodes.name: Little-o estimate at a density point of the critical set
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon E \to F\) be a function from a finite dimensional real normed space to a real normed space. Consider a set \(s\) and a point \(a\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(f\) is \(C^{1+(\alpha)}\) at \(a\); \item \(Df(x)=0\) for each \(x\in s\); \item \(a\in s\) is a Lebesgue density point of \(s\). \end{itemize} Then \(f(x)-f(a)=o\left(\left\|x - a\right\|^{1+\alpha}\right)\) as \(x\to a\).
assumptions: Let \(f\colon E \to F\) be a function from a finite dimensional real normed space to a real normed space
\(Df(x)=0\) for each \(x\in s\)
\(a\in s\) is a Lebesgue density point of \(s\)
conclusions: \(f(x)-f(a)=o\left(\left\|x - a\right\|^{1+\alpha}\right)\) as \(x\to a\)
nodes.statement_short: At a Lebesgue density point of a set where $Df=0$, a $C^{1+(\alpha)}$ map satisfies $f(x)-f(a)=o(\|x-a\|^{1+\alpha})$.
nodes.label: cor:cdh-at-isLittleO-of-density

nodes.name: Proof of Little-o estimate at a density point of the critical set
nodes.statement: Take \(C\) such that \(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\) for \(x\) sufficiently close to \(a\). It suffices to show that for every \(\epsilon > 0\), we have \(\|f(x) - f(a)\| \le 2C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{1+\alpha}\) for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(a\). Choose \(\delta > 0\) such that for any set \(T\) of measure at least \((1-\delta)\mu(B_{1})\) in a unit ball, for each point \(x\) on the unit sphere there exists another point \(y\) on the sphere such that \(\|x - y\| \le \epsilon\) and the measure of \(t\in [0, 1]\) such that \(x+t(y - x)\in T\) is at least \(1 - \epsilon\). Existence of \(\delta > 0\) with these properties follows from \autoref{cor:meas-ball-gt-pos} Then choose \(R>0\) such that \(s\) occupies at least \(1-\delta\) fraction of the volume of a ball \(B_{r}(a)\) for all \(0 < r < R\) and the estimate \(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\) holds on \(B_{R}(a)\). Take \(x\in B_{R}(a)\). Find \(y\) such that \(\|y - a\| = \|x - a\|\), \(\|y - x\| \le \epsilon\|x - a\|\), and the measure of \(t\in [0, 1]\) such that \(a + t(y - a)\in s\) is at least \(1 - \epsilon\). Then \(\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\|x - y\| \le C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{\alpha+1}\) due to the Mean Value Theorem. On the other hand, \autoref{cor:cdh-at-sub-le-of-meas-fderiv} implies that \(\|f(y) - f(a)\| \le C\epsilon\|y - a\|^{\alpha+1}\). Finally, the triangle inequality implies that \(\|f(x) - f(a)\| \le 2C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{\alpha+1}\).
nodes.statement_short: For each $\epsilon$, pass from $x$ to a nearby point $y$ at equal distance whose segment to $a$ lies mostly in $s$. Mean value theorem bounds $f(x)-f(y)$, the measure-based increment bound handles $f(y)-f(a)$, then the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Fix the Hölder constant $C$
nodes.statement: Take \(C\) such that \(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\) for \(x\) sufficiently close to \(a\). It suffices to show that for every \(\epsilon > 0\), we have \(\|f(x) - f(a)\| \le 2C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{1+\alpha}\) for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(a\).
nodes.statement_short: Fix the Hölder constant $C$; reduce to a $2C\epsilon$ bound

nodes.name: Choose $\delta$ via the uniform ball-measure bound
nodes.statement: Choose \(\delta > 0\) such that for any set \(T\) of measure at least \((1-\delta)\mu(B_{1})\) in a unit ball, for each point \(x\) on the unit sphere there exists another point \(y\) on the sphere such that \(\|x - y\| \le \epsilon\) and the measure of \(t\in [0, 1]\) such that \(x+t(y - x)\in T\) is at least \(1 - \epsilon\). Existence of \(\delta > 0\) with these properties follows from \autoref{cor:meas-ball-gt-pos}
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\delta$ via the uniform ball-measure bound

nodes.name: Choose radius $R$ from density and the derivative bound
nodes.statement: Then choose \(R>0\) such that \(s\) occupies at least \(1-\delta\) fraction of the volume of a ball \(B_{r}(a)\) for all \(0 < r < R\) and the estimate \(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\) holds on \(B_{R}(a)\).
nodes.statement_short: Choose radius $R$ from density and the derivative bound

nodes.name: Pick $x$ and the companion point $y$
nodes.statement: Take \(x\in B_{R}(a)\). Find \(y\) such that \(\|y - a\| = \|x - a\|\), \(\|y - x\| \le \epsilon\|x - a\|\), and the measure of \(t\in [0, 1]\) such that \(a + t(y - a)\in s\) is at least \(1 - \epsilon\).
nodes.statement_short: Pick $x$ and the companion point $y$

nodes.name: Mean value theorem bounds $f(x)-f(y)$
nodes.statement: Then \(\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le C\|x - a\|^{\alpha}\|x - y\| \le C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{\alpha+1}\) due to the Mean Value Theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem bounds $f(x)-f(y)$

nodes.name: Increment bound gives $f(y)-f(a)$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \autoref{cor:cdh-at-sub-le-of-meas-fderiv} implies that \(\|f(y) - f(a)\| \le C\epsilon\|y - a\|^{\alpha+1}\).
nodes.statement_short: Increment bound gives $f(y)-f(a)$

nodes.name: Triangle inequality concludes
nodes.statement: Finally, the triangle inequality implies that \(\|f(x) - f(a)\| \le 2C\epsilon\|x - a\|^{\alpha+1}\).
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality concludes

nodes.name: Power-type increment bound on a convex set
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon E\to F\) be a function between real normed spaces. Suppose that \(f\) is differentiable in a neighborhood of \(a \in E\) and \(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{r}\) on a convex set \(s \ni a\). Then \(\|f(x) - f(a)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{r + 1}\) for \(x\in s\).
assumptions: \(f\colon E\to F\) be a function between real normed spaces
\(f\) is differentiable in a neighborhood of \(a \in E\)
\(\|Df(x)\|\le C\|x - a\|^{r}\) on a convex set \(s \ni a\)
nodes.label: cor:cdh-at-sub-le

nodes.name: Proof of Power-type increment bound on a convex set
nodes.statement: This statement immediately follows from \autoref{cor:cdh-at-sub-le-of-meas-fderiv} for \(\delta = 1\).
nodes.statement_short: Take $\delta=1$ in the increment bound.

nodes.statement: If \(f\colon E \to F\) is \(C^{1}\) at \(a \in E\) and \(\|Df(x)\|=o\left(\left\|x - a\right\|^{r}\right)\) as \(x\to a\), where \(r\ge 0\), then \(\|x - a\| = o\left(\left\|x - a\right\|^{r + 1}\right)\) as \(x\to a\).

\(\|Df(x)\|=o\left(\left\|x - a\right\|^{r}\right)\) as \(x\to a\)
where \(r\ge 0\)

nodes.statement: The statement immediately follows from \autoref{cor:cdh-at-sub-le}.

nodes.name: Big-O estimate along a Moreira chart
nodes.statement: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\). Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\). Let \(f\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n}\to F\) be a function such that \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((s, U)\). Then for any \((a, b)\in t_{k}\), we have \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=O\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\).
assumptions: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\)
Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\)
conclusions: \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=O\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\)
nodes.statement_short: Along a depth-$k$ $C^{k+(\alpha)}$ Moreira chart, $f\circ\Psi_k$ varies as $O(\|y-b\|^{k+\alpha})$ at points of $t_k$.
nodes.label: thm:moreira-chart-isBigO

nodes.name: Proof of Big-O estimate along a Moreira chart
nodes.statement: We prove it by induction on \(k\). The induction base \(k = 1\) follows from the definition of a \(C^{1+(\alpha)}\) function, and the induction step follows from \autoref{cor:sub-isLittleO-rpow-of-fderiv}
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$: base from the definition, step from the little-o increment corollary.

nodes.name: Little-o estimate along a Moreira chart at density points
nodes.statement: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\). Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\), \(k > 0\). Let \(f\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n}\to F\) be a function such that \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((s, U)\). Consider \((a, b)\in t_{k}\) such that \(b\) is a Lebesgue density point of the closure of the set \(\{y\mid (a, y)\in t_{k}\}\). Then \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=o\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\).
assumptions: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\)
Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\), \(k > 0\)
Consider \((a, b)\in t_{k}\) such that \(b\) is a Lebesgue density point of the closure of the set \(\{y\mid (a, y)\in t_{k}\}\)
conclusions: \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=o\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\)
nodes.statement_short: At fibrewise density points of $t_k$, $f\circ\Psi_k$ varies as $o(\|y-b\|^{k+\alpha})$.
nodes.label: thm:moreira-chart-isLittleO

nodes.name: Proof of Little-o estimate along a Moreira chart at density points
nodes.statement: We prove it by induction on \(k\). The induction base \(k = 1\) follows from \autoref{cor:cdh-at-isLittleO-of-density} while the induction step follows from \autoref{cor:sub-isLittleO-rpow-of-fderiv}
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$: base from the density-point corollary, step from the little-o increment corollary.

nodes.name: Almost-everywhere little-o estimate along a Moreira chart
nodes.statement: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\). Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\), \(k > 0\). Let \(f\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n}\to F\) be a function such that \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((s, U)\). Then for a.e.\ \((a, b) \in t_{k}\), \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=o\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\).
assumptions: Consider \(s\subset U\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n}\)
Consider a Moreira chart of \((s, U)\) of smoothness \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) of depth \(k\), \(k > 0\)
conclusions: for a.e.\ \((a, b) \in t_{k}\), \(f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, y)) - f(a, \Psi_{k}(a, b))=o\left(\|y - b\|^{k + \alpha}\right)\) as \(y\to b\)
nodes.statement_short: For a.e. point of $t_k$, $f\circ\Psi_k$ varies as $o(\|y-b\|^{k+\alpha})$.
nodes.label: cor:moreira-chart-ae-isLittleO

nodes.name: Proof of Almost-everywhere little-o estimate along a Moreira chart
nodes.statement: This fact immediately follows from \autoref{thm:moreira-chart-isLittleO}, \autoref{cor:measurable-density}, and the Lebesgue density theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the density-point estimate with measurability of density points and the Lebesgue density theorem.

nodes.name: Moreira covering
nodes.statement: Let \(E\) be a real normed space, let \(n\) be a natural number. Consider a set \(s\subset E \times \mathbb R^{n}\) and its open neighborhood \(U\supset s\). A \emph{Moreira covering} of \((s, U)\) of depth \(l\) is a countable collection of Moreira charts of depth \(l\) such that the union of the sets \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \Psi_{l}(x, y)))(t_{l})\) is the whole \(s\).
nodes.genus: countable collection of Moreira charts of depth \(l\)
differentia: the union of the sets \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \Psi_{l}(x, y)))(t_{l})\) is the whole \(s\)
nodes.label: def:moreira-covering

nodes.name: Existence of a Moreira covering of depth 0
nodes.statement: If \(E\) is a real normed space with second-countable topology and \(n\) is a natural number, then every pair \((s, U)\) in \(E\times\mathbb R^{n}\) admits a Moreira covering of depth \(0\).
assumptions: \(E\) is a real normed space with second-countable topology and \(n\) is a natural number
conclusions: every pair \((s, U)\) in \(E\times\mathbb R^{n}\) admits a Moreira covering of depth \(0\)
nodes.label: lem:moreira-covering-zero

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of a Moreira covering of depth 0
nodes.statement: This lemma follows immediately from the definitions and the fact that a second countable topological space is hereditarily Lindelof.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold definitions and use that second countable spaces are hereditarily Lindelöf.

nodes.name: Existence of a Moreira covering of depth 1
nodes.statement: If \(E\) is a real normed space with second-countable topology and \(n\) is a natural number, then every pair \((s, U)\) in \(E\times\mathbb R^{n}\) admits a Moreira covering of depth \(1\).
assumptions: \(E\) is a real normed space with second-countable topology and \(n\) is a natural number
conclusions: every pair \((s, U)\) in \(E\times\mathbb R^{n}\) admits a Moreira covering of depth \(1\)
nodes.label: lem:moreira-covering-one

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of a Moreira covering of depth 1
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction on \(n\). Let \(t \subset s\) be the set of points \((x, y)\in s\) such that there exists a function \(f\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n}\to \mathbb R\) such that \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((s, U)\), \(\left.f\right|_{s}=0\), and \(D_{2}f\ne 0\). For each \((a, b)\in s\), we use \autoref{thm:cdh-at-implicit-dichotomy} to find a function \(\psi\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\to \mathbb R^{n}\), open balls \(B\subset E\) and \(V\subset\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) with centers \(x\) and \(0\), and a set \(u\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(\psi\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((u, B\times V)\); \item \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \psi(x, y)))(u)\) is a neighborhood of \((a, b)\) within \(s\); \item \(\psi(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V\) for each \(x\in B\). \end{itemize} The latter condition can be satisfied by composing \(\psi\) with a homoethety. Then we apply the inductive assumption to \((u, B\times V)\) and compose each chart with \(\psi\). For each \((a, b)\in s \setminus t\), we choose open balls \(B\) and \(V\) with centers \(a\) and \(b\) such that \(B\times V\subset U\), then take \(\psi(x, y) = y\) and \((s \setminus t)\cap (B\times V)\) as a chart and its domain, respectively. Charts of the first type cover \(t\) and charts of the second type cover \(s \setminus t\), thus their union covers the whole \(s\).
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$, covering points with a nondegenerate vanishing function by implicit-function charts and the rest by trivial charts. Implicit-function dichotomy charts are rescaled to be expanding, then refined by the inductive hypothesis.

nodes.name: Induction on $n$
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction on \(n\). Let \(t \subset s\) be the set of points \((x, y)\in s\) such that there exists a function \(f\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n}\to \mathbb R\) such that \(f\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((s, U)\), \(\left.f\right|_{s}=0\), and \(D_{2}f\ne 0\).
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $n$; define the nondegenerate set $t$

nodes.name: Charts from the implicit function dichotomy
nodes.statement: For each \((a, b)\in s\), we use \autoref{thm:cdh-at-implicit-dichotomy} to find a function \(\psi\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\to \mathbb R^{n}\), open balls \(B\subset E\) and \(V\subset\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) with centers \(x\) and \(0\), and a set \(u\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(\psi\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((u, B\times V)\); \item \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \psi(x, y)))(u)\) is a neighborhood of \((a, b)\) within \(s\); \item \(\psi(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V\) for each \(x\in B\). \end{itemize} The latter condition can be satisfied by composing \(\psi\) with a homoethety. Then we apply the inductive assumption to \((u, B\times V)\) and compose each chart with \(\psi\).
nodes.statement_short: Charts from the implicit function dichotomy

nodes.name: Apply the dichotomy to get $\psi$, balls, set $u$
nodes.statement: For each \((a, b)\in s\), we use \autoref{thm:cdh-at-implicit-dichotomy} to find a function \(\psi\colon E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\to \mathbb R^{n}\), open balls \(B\subset E\) and \(V\subset\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) with centers \(x\) and \(0\), and a set \(u\subset E\times\mathbb R^{n - 1}\) such that \begin{itemize} \item \(\psi\) is \(C^{k+(\alpha)}\) on \((u, B\times V)\); \item \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \psi(x, y)))(u)\) is a neighborhood of \((a, b)\) within \(s\); \item \(\psi(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V\) for each \(x\in B\).

nodes.statement_short: Dichotomy gives a $C^{k+(\alpha)}$ map $\psi$

nodes.name: Its graph map covers a neighbourhood in $s$
nodes.statement: \(((x, y) \mapsto (x, \psi(x, y)))(u)\) is a neighborhood of \((a, b)\) within \(s\);
nodes.statement_short: Its graph map covers a neighbourhood in $s$

nodes.name: $\psi$ is expanding
nodes.statement: \(\psi(x, y)\) is expanding in \(y\) on \(V\) for each \(x\in B\).
nodes.statement_short: $\psi$ is expanding

nodes.name: Achieve expansion by a homothety
nodes.statement: The latter condition can be satisfied by composing \(\psi\) with a homoethety.
nodes.statement_short: Achieve expansion by a homothety

nodes.name: Apply the inductive hypothesis and compose
nodes.statement: Then we apply the inductive assumption to \((u, B\times V)\) and compose each chart with \(\psi\).
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inductive hypothesis and compose

nodes.name: Trivial charts on $s\setminus t$
nodes.statement: For each \((a, b)\in s \setminus t\), we choose open balls \(B\) and \(V\) with centers \(a\) and \(b\) such that \(B\times V\subset U\), then take \(\psi(x, y) = y\) and \((s \setminus t)\cap (B\times V)\) as a chart and its domain, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial charts on $s\setminus t$

nodes.name: The two families cover $s$
nodes.statement: Charts of the first type cover \(t\) and charts of the second type cover \(s \setminus t\), thus their union covers the whole \(s\).
nodes.statement_short: The two families cover $s$

nodes.name: Existence of Moreira coverings of any depth
nodes.statement: In the assumptions of the previous lemma, \((s, U)\) admits a Moreira covering of any depth \(l \le k\).
assumptions: In the assumptions of the previous lemma
conclusions: \((s, U)\) admits a Moreira covering of any depth \(l \le k\)
nodes.label: thm:moreira-covering-exists

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of Moreira coverings of any depth
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction on \(l\). The induction base is given by \autoref{lem:moreira-covering-zero}. For the induction step, use \autoref{lem:moreira-covering-one} to get a Moreira covering of depth \(1\), then take a Moreira covering of depth \(l\) for each \((t, B\times V)\) in this covering, then compose them.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $l$: depth-0 base, then refine a depth-1 covering by depth-$l$ coverings and compose.
